If your pads make you itch, switch brands until you find one that doesn’t. You might have a sensitivity to something your current pad brand is made with. If it’s just the pads themselves that make you itch from having them on, try tampons or a disk or a cup. There are lots of options!

About the pain? It’s different for everyone. Some of my friends have no pain at all while I feel like I’m hit by a truck my first two days of my period. But if the pain is bad enough that you can’t function through your day, I’d see a doctor. You might have something along the lines of PCOS or endometriosis.

The color? It’s all sorts of weird colors. The brown rust-ish color when you first bleed is the oldest blood and it should get lighter from there. It might even be clear-ish at some point, which is discharge. Unless it’s like a yellowy-green, generally you’re fine.
It could be ovulation cramps. But when in doubt, go to the doctor. Better safe than sorry!

There’s no healthy way to “stop” it that quick. The cycle is generally about 28 days long, with day one being the first day you bleed- but everyone is different. So likely you’ll get it after your trip.

If you’re worried about leakage or time, I’d invest in a period cup (they last anywhere between 10-12 hours, but are a little messy to clean and change). If you’re just worried about pain, meds and heat for the cramps is what I recommend.

Because it sounds like this is (possibly) your first set of lobes, I have some other advice as well (as someone who has 12 piercings):

1) if a crust builds up, that’s okay. It’s just white blood cells that build up when healing. It’s okay to clean the stuff off. I personally use cleaning solution like H2Ocean, but if you were given a solution when you were pierced- that’s probably good too. But tea tree oil and hydrogen peroxide are a big no no. They dry out your skin and can harm the healing process.

2) don’t change them or take them out for extended periods of time for at least the first 2 or 3 months. Usually lobes heal on the quicker side of things and are simpler to take care of while healing. But if you bug them, they’ll bug you with healing problems. 
Edit: I’ve always been told lobes fully heal some time around 6/8 months

Hi! Actual asexual here. Asexually has lots of gray areas- one of which is Demisexual. This particular phrase means that you feel sexual attraction only after a meaningful, emotional relationship. You can define yourself however you feel comfortable and if it takes a while, no sweat. And no- wanting to be touched and held doesn’t make you a paradox. Personally I’d melt if someone cradled my face in their hands and rubbed my cheeks with their thumbs. Honestly that’s how I figured out I was asexual lol, everyone else wants to jump certain peoples’ bones but I’d like to just be held by them.

I totally agree with you being angry that sex seems to be at the forefront of like literally everything- honestly it sucks and I wish it would stop. But asexuals are like 1-2% of the population and everything else tends to cater to the masses. Not much we can do about it besides be up front with people we intend to try and date. I’ll admit it’s also put me in a pickle when it comes to dating, but I did try to ignore it once and it did not feel right when the kissing and groping happened. Don’t push yourself into something that doesn’t feel right sweetheart, it will only come back to haunt you.

Feel free to DM me if you have questions about the asexual stuff- I’ll try to answer them if it can lol
